title: Product PRD: Unified Inference — Overview, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Daniel Morgan
body:
Executive summary:

This doc consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design, roadmap & themes, pricing/packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference initiative (hosted + dedicated + private). The goal is to provide a single reference for product managers, engineering, and GTM to align on what ships in 2026 Q1–Q3 and how we measure success.

1) Problem statement
- Customers run into inconsistent performance and operational complexity when moving models between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Cost and latency trade-offs are opaque; platform teams need deterministic controls for latency SLOs and unit economics.

2) Goals (OKRs)
- O1: Deliver a single API surface that supports predictable latency across deployment modes (SLO: median p95 latency delta < 15% vs hosted).
- O2: Reduce per-token serving cost for common workloads by 20% via batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations.
- O3: Enable enterprise adoption with Private deployment hardened for compliance (SOC2 + regional data residency) by end of Q2.

3) Scope
- In scope: API contract refinements, model routing & fallback policies, per-route observability, standard batching/caching profiles, pricing models for Dedicated and Private, rollout playbooks and release.
- Out of scope: New model training pipelines, third-party marketplace integrations (post-Q3).

4) Product requirements (MUST / SHOULD / MAY)
- MUST: Unified REST/SDK contract (text, chat, embeddings, tool-calling) with versioned model selection.
- MUST: Policy-driven routing: latency-first, cost-first, regulatory-bound routes.
- MUST: Observable per-route SLOs with token-level cost breakdown in Console.
- MUST: Dedicated pricing tier with reserved capacity contracts and predictable billing.
- SHOULD: Automatic quantization profile suggestions per workload.
- SHOULD: Built-in canary rollouts and automatic rollback on quality regressions.
- MAY: Marketplace for model variants (deferred).

5) Requirements matrix (nominal config table)
| Requirement | Owner | Acceptance criteria | Priority |
|---|---|---:|---|
| API parity across modes | API team | Same endpoints + 0 breaking changes for GA | MUST |
| Routing & fallback | Serving Runtime | 99.9% successful fallback under overload | MUST |
| Per-route cost visibility | Console | Token cost shown within 1h of usage | MUST |
| Dedicated reserved billing | Finance & Sales | Support monthly/yearly commits and overruns | MUST |
| Quantization recommendations | Research | >10% cost saving on target workloads | SHOULD |

6) Design overview
- Architecture: control plane (model catalog, routing policies, billing) + data plane (hosted inference fleet, dedicated pools, private connectors).
- Smart routing: policy engine evaluates (latency_budget, cost_target, region, customer_tier); if primary model unavailable, fallback to nearest compatible variant (quantized, smaller architecture).
- Caching & batching: per-customer prefix KV cache, adaptive batching with latency-aware windows, and model-specific batching profiles.
- Observability: trace/span hooks at request lifecycle, token-level telemetry, per-route dashboards in Console.

7) API examples (reference)
- Generation request (REST): POST /v1/generate {"model":"redwood-unified-v1","input":"...","route_policy":"latency_first"}
- Routing policy sample (YAML):
route_policy:
  name: latency_first
  priority: ["latency","region","cost"]
  fallbacks: ["redwood-unified-v1-quant","redwood-unified-v0.9"]

8) Roadmap & themes (Q2–Q4 2026)
- Q2 2026 (Stabilize & Enterprise):
  - GA: Unified API parity (text/chat/embeddings) across hosted and dedicated.
  - Private beta for SOC2 customers and selected regulated verticals.
  - Pricing: Reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual).
- Q3 2026 (Optimize & Scale):
  - Quantization profile recommendations and auto-config optimizer (Redwood Optimize v6).
  - Improved fallbacks and multi-region routing for 99.95% availability during partial outages.
  - SDKs: expanded language clients and better streaming semantics.
- Q4 2026 (Enterprise & Ecosystem):
  - Private GA and marketplace pilot for certified model variants.
  - Advanced observability: custom metric import and long-term retention add-on.

9) Pricing & packaging guidance
- Hosted API: usage-based pricing (tokens) with free-tier credits for devs.
- Dedicated: two tiers — Standard (shared pools but dedicated compute) and Reserved (customer-dedicated GPU pools) with commit discounts.
- Private: Platform fee + node-based licensing + optional premium support / compliance add-ons.

Pricing examples (illustrative):
| Plan | Billing model | Highlights |
|---|---|---|
| Developer (Hosted) | per-token | Free tier 100k tokens/mo, pay-as-you-go |
| Dedicated Standard | monthly seat | Base monthly + usage overage at discounted rate |
| Dedicated Reserved | annual commit | 20–40% commit discount, SLA-backed latency targets |
| Private | license + infra | One-time onboarding + annual license + support tier |

10) Packaging notes for Sales & Finance
- Offer 3 common SKUs: Developer (hosted), Dedicated (Standard/Reserved), Private (Core + Compliance).
- Standard contract templates in /finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process.
- Billing flows: meter hosted usage hourly, Dedicated commit amortized monthly, Private invoiced per contract.

11) Launch plan & rollout (high level)
1. Feature freeze and internal dogfood (2 weeks).
2. Private beta with 3 enterprise customers (4 weeks).
3. Collect performance & quality metrics; run automated regressions on canonical prompt sets.
4. Gradual public rollout via feature-flag (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%), monitor SLOs and error budgets.
5. GTM enablement: publish pricing page, updated SDKs, sample integration templates.

12) Metrics / KPIs & SLOs
- Latency SLO (per-route): p95 < 600ms for short text workloads (<=512 tokens) for latency_first routes.
- Availability SLO: 99.95% regional availability for Dedicated Reserved.
- Cost KPI: average cost per 1k tokens down 20% vs baseline in production.
- Quality KPI: prompt set pass rate >=95% for regression suite post-release.

13) Ownership and stakeholders
- Product lead: Daniel Morgan (product).
- Eng leads: Priya Narang (serving runtime), Ethan Park (console & observability).
- Research: Marisol Vega (quantization & evals).
- Sales & Finance: contact via sales-enablement/pitch-decks.

14) Release notes (v1.3.0 — 2026-03-04)
- Version: v1.3.0 (Unified Inference GA candidate)
- Date: 2026-03-04
- Notable changes:
  - Unified API: text, chat, and embeddings endpoints reached parity across hosted and dedicated.
  - Routing: policy-driven routing engine (latency_first, cost_first) and automatic fallbacks to quantized variants.
  - Console: per-route token cost breakdown and per-model latency histograms.
  - Pricing: Dedicated Reserved SKU introduced (monthly/annual commit options).
  - Private: early beta with SOC2 compliance checklist and enterprise onboarding playbook.
- Known issues:
  - Private installer does not yet support on-prem air-gapped PKI rotation (planned Q3).
  - Quantization recommendations are conservative for larger seq-len workloads; accuracy tuning in progress.

15) Post-release actions (owners & due dates)
- 2026-03-11: Run QPS soak test at 2x projected load (Priya Narang).
- 2026-03-18: Validate billing reconciliation for Dedicated Reserved (Finance).
- 2026-04-01: Expand private beta to 10 customers and begin compliance evidence collection (Security & Customer Success).
